## Company Overview

Quilliam AI is the trading name of Quilliam AI Ltd, a UK private limited company registered in England and Wales under Companies House number 17151006. The company was incorporated on 2026-04-11. Its registered office is 25 Red Cove Close, St. Eval, Wadebridge, PL27 7GB. Levi Lachlan Quilliam is the founder, sole director and sole shareholder.

Quilliam AI is based in Cornwall and provides AI assessment, staff training and implementation services throughout the United Kingdom. The company reviews defined business processes, identifies suitable uses of AI, implements agreed workflows or supervised agents and trains the staff responsible for operating them.

Each paid engagement is governed by an agreed scope, deliverables, responsibilities, controls, timetable and fee. Documentation and handover requirements are included where applicable so that the client can operate and review the delivered system.

## Approach

Quilliam AI begins with a defined business process. The assessment considers frequency, current cost, delay, system dependencies, available data, risk and responsible staff. A suitable project should have an accountable owner, representative test cases and measurable acceptance criteria.

Where implementation is justified, Quilliam AI defines the trigger, required context, permitted actions, approval requirements, access restrictions, logging, fallback procedures and responsibility for ongoing review. The first release is tested against representative cases before wider use. Staff training and handover documents cover the agreed operation, controls and maintenance procedures.

An initial recommendation may include implementation, a supervised agent, staff training, data preparation or deferral. The recommendation depends on the evidence available and the expected business benefit.

---

## Services

### AI Opportunity Analysis

AI Opportunity Analysis is an assessment of recurring business processes and their suitability for AI. Quilliam AI reviews the current method, systems, data, staff responsibilities, volume, delay, quality requirements and risk. The resulting recommendation identifies suitable opportunities in priority order and records any preparation required before implementation. It also states the proposed scope, controls, accountable owner and measure of success for the first project. The assessment may recommend a workflow, a supervised agent, staff training, data preparation or deferral. This service is intended for business owners and operational leads who require a reasoned basis for deciding whether to commit time and budget to AI work.

### Team Training

Team Training provides role-specific instruction on the use of AI in current business processes. Training may cover approved tools, prompt preparation, source material, checking output, privacy, confidential information, internal policy, escalation and human approval. Examples are based on the roles and processes included in the agreed scope. Written guidance may include prompts, review checklists, process instructions and rules for permitted or restricted use. The objective is consistent and accountable use by the relevant staff. A free introductory AI training session is available to discuss the team, current level of use and proposed training requirement.

### AI Implementation

AI Implementation covers the design, implementation, testing and handover of AI workflows, automations, supervised agents, knowledge systems and internal tools. Typical processes include lead intake, customer follow-up, support triage, weekly reporting, research, document handling, internal knowledge and administration across email, documents, CRM systems and spreadsheets. The implementation is based on an agreed process and may use n8n, APIs, forms, databases and AI models such as Claude or ChatGPT. Controls may include restricted permissions, limited data access, human approval, audit logs, test cases and fallback procedures. The responsible staff receive the agreed training and handover documents before release.

### Supervised AI Agents

A supervised AI agent performs a defined task within stated permissions and approval requirements. It may retrieve authorised information, classify a request, prepare a proposed action or update an agreed system. Human approval is retained for actions carrying material risk. Typical examples include lead qualification, support triage, research, internal knowledge retrieval, CRM maintenance and operational reporting. Each agent requires an accountable owner, test cases, monitoring and a documented fallback procedure.

---

## Case Study | VetVision AI

VetVision AI is a University of Nottingham spin-out that uses camera systems to monitor animal welfare in equine and dairy environments. Quilliam AI has supported the presentation of the AI product, search content, customer onboarding, farm and camera operations, and defined internal uses of AI.

The work included consolidating two brands under the VetVision AI name, revising the website, developing a branded onboarding portal and documenting processes for farm mapping, camera placement and camera replacement planning.

Reported outcomes include an approximate website SEO score change from 40 to 95 and increases in search visibility, visitor numbers and enquiries. These figures are reported as project outcomes and are not a guarantee of results for other clients.

---

## Delivery Process

### 1. Assess current processes
Quilliam AI reviews recurring administration, follow-up, customer enquiries, reporting, document handling and handovers. The assessment records the current process, cost or delay, responsible staff, systems, data and risk.

### 2. Define the first project
The proposed scope states the trigger, required context, actions, approvals, permissions, logs, fallback procedures, owner, risk and success measures. A written scope and fee are provided before paid work begins.

### 3. Implement and test
Quilliam AI connects the agreed models, tools and data, applies the required controls and tests the system against representative cases. Release depends on the agreed acceptance criteria.

### 4. Train and hand over
The responsible staff receive training and documentation covering operation, output review, controls, escalation, fallback procedures and agreed maintenance responsibilities.

---

## Suitable Engagements

Relevant clients may include:
- Small and growing businesses with recurring administration, follow-up, reporting or customer support work
- Agencies and consultancies seeking to improve delivery processes
- Start-ups and scale-ups establishing defined AI operating procedures
- Teams within larger organisations conducting an AI pilot
- Owner-led businesses requiring direct access to the principal consultant

Initial suitability indicators include:
- The same type of task occurs regularly
- Examples, policies, rules or repeated patterns are available
- A named person is accountable for the outcome
- The current time, cost, delay or quality issue can be measured
- Representative cases are available for testing

## Founder | Levi Quilliam

Levi Quilliam is the founder and sole director of Quilliam AI Ltd. He holds a Bachelor's degree in Economics and a Graduate Certificate in Computer Science. His professional experience includes turnaround and restructuring at Deloitte, followed by technology roles at Halter. He has more than eight years of experience in software, AI tools, integrations, automation and product workflows.

This combination of business and technical experience informs the assessment of process, cost, responsibility, risk and implementation requirements for each engagement.

## Budget Guidance

Quilliam AI quotes against an agreed scope. The fee depends on the process, data, systems, risk, testing, training and handover requirements. Training usually starts from £500. Small implementation projects may cost approximately £2,000 to £3,000. Medium projects may range from £5,000 to £50,000. Larger programmes are usually above £50,000. Ongoing support may be agreed where a system requires monitoring, maintenance or further development.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What services does Quilliam AI provide?
Quilliam AI provides AI Opportunity Analysis, role-specific staff training and implementation of AI workflows, automations, supervised agents, knowledge systems and internal tools.

### What is an AI Opportunity Session?
An AI Opportunity Session is a free initial discussion about a current business process and whether it may be suitable for AI. The session identifies the proposed next step and likely scope. A detailed assessment or implementation is subject to a separate written agreement.

### Does Quilliam AI train staff?
Yes. Training is based on the roles, policies and business processes included in the agreed scope. It covers appropriate use, preparation, output review, privacy, controls and escalation.

### Does Quilliam AI implement automations?
Yes. Quilliam AI implements AI workflows, n8n automations, API integrations, knowledge systems, internal tools and supervised agents where there is an agreed business case.

### How are AI risks controlled?
Controls are selected according to the process and risk. They may include restricted permissions, limited data access, human approval, representative test cases, audit logs, fallback procedures and named owners.

### Where does Quilliam AI work?
Quilliam AI is based in Cornwall and provides remote and in-person services throughout the United Kingdom. In-person sessions are available by agreement.
